E1.evidence: Reporter gives a reproduction setup (Turtlebot3 + gazebo + nav2_smac_planner Hybrid A*, full parameter file) and images; maintainer confirms: "I can reproduce that on Jazzy myself when using the default parameters in the [Docs](https://docs.nav2.org/configuration/packages/smac/configuring-smac-hybrid.html) with the change of using the Reeds-Shepp model rather than Dubins" -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5192

E2.evidence: The defect is inside nav2_smac_planner's own search/analytic-expansion logic (the Reeds-Shepp analytic expansion and its refinement stage choose a path with a one-point reverse segment at the junction with the forward search). Maintainer: "it is the Reeds-Shepp paths legit have the extra backup-and-then-move-forward behavior. While most of the time I see it happen due to the turning radius refinement stage, I can also see it normally happen in the raw Reeds-Shepp path that is generated by OMPL as the shortest possible path." The fixes (PR #5198 bool/float score and parent-linking fix in analytic_expansion.cpp; PR #5207/#5216 constraint on directional changes during refinement) change only nav2_smac_planner's internal algorithm (plus bringup launch files). No value, frame, unit, name or timing crosses a unit boundary incorrectly; the output path would be the same with any correct peer (planner server, controller or OMPL). -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5192 Other defects in the thread: Issue 1 (refineAnalyticPath float score assigned to bool, wrong parent association after refinement; PR #5198) and another user's lattice-planner wrong-goal report (tested against PR #5235) are also internal to nav2_smac_planner.

E3.evidence: Not evaluated past E2; the planner produces the path within its own process (PAIR with a path consumer would be the only candidate operation).

E4.evidence: Observed path with a backward-then-forward point at the analytic-expansion junction, shown in images and videos in the issue.
